addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state or plan that logic shared by files, crates or tools lives in one place they all use (a shared module, crate, or the client template from which code is generated), or that existing duplicated logic is moved into such a place? Judge presence of that statement only, not conflict. An item that simply does not copy anything but says nothing about shared logic has not stated it.

criteria.yes: The item says two or more files, crates or tools use one shared implementation (for example 'both tools call the shared client generated from the template', 'move the duplicated parser into the shared module', 'regenerate the client in both tools from the shared template').
criteria.no: The item says nothing about sharing one implementation: it is silent, adds tool-specific code, only mentions the topic, or copies code.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at sharing but it cannot be told whether one shared implementation is used.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor logic from one file, crate or tool into another, so the same logic exists in two places? Regenerating code from one shared template is not copying. An item that is silent about copying does not plan it.

criteria.yes: The item plans to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor a function, parser or other logic from one file, crate or tool into another.
criteria.no: The item plans no such copy: it is silent, shares one implementation, generates code from one template, or adds logic with no counterpart elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item could be read as duplicating logic, but it is ambiguous.

relevant.instructions: Decide whether `item.text` describes code in an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use. Answer yes when the item plans or describes how such code is written, changed, copied, generated, or what it calls or shares. Answer no when the item does no code work at all: documentation, plan notes, CI configuration, tracker work, or a meeting or discussion, even if that item talks about these tools or about duplicated code.

criteria.yes: The item plans or describes code in an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use: writing, changing, copying, generating it, or what it calls or shares.
criteria.no: The item does no code work: documentation, plan notes, CI configuration, tracker work, a meeting or discussion, or it concerns code outside these crates and tools.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told whether the item involves code in these crates, tools or the template.

anchor.statement: sc-agent, judge-jev and plan-anchor code must not copy and paste logic between files or tools, so the code base does not grow unnecessarily.
anchor.scope: adds or changes source code in sc-agent crates (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr and the other crates/ members), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use; adds a helper, parser or function that does the same job as one in another file or tool; copies, ports or vendors code from one file, crate or tool into another

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state or plan that logic shared by files, crates or tools lives in one place they all use (a shared module, crate, or the client template from which code is generated), or that existing duplicated logic is moved into such a place? Judge presence of that statement only, not conflict. An item that simply does not copy anything but says nothing about shared logic has not stated it.

criteria.yes: The item says two or more files, crates or tools use one shared implementation (for example 'both tools call the shared client generated from the template', 'move the duplicated parser into the shared module', 'regenerate the client in both tools from the shared template').
criteria.no: The item says nothing about sharing one implementation: it is silent, adds tool-specific code, only mentions the topic, or copies code.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at sharing but it cannot be told whether one shared implementation is used.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor logic from one file, crate or tool into another, so the same logic exists in two places? Regenerating code from one shared template is not copying. An item that is silent about copying does not plan it.

criteria.yes: The item plans to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor a function, parser or other logic from one file, crate or tool into another.
criteria.no: The item plans no such copy: it is silent, shares one implementation, generates code from one template, or adds logic with no counterpart elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item could be read as duplicating logic, but it is ambiguous.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` about the code of an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use? Code work counts in any form: adding, changing, copying, porting, vendoring or regenerating code, adding a helper, parser or function, or stating which shared code these tools call. Work that touches no code - documentation, notes in a plan, CI configuration, tracker work, discussions - is not about the code, even when it names the tools or the topic of duplication.

criteria.yes: The item does or describes code work in these crates, tools or the shared template, including stating which shared code they call.
criteria.no: The item touches no code in these crates, tools or the template: it is documentation, a plan note, CI configuration, tracker work or a discussion, or code elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions these tools but it cannot be told whether it involves their code.
